claims.claim: WPS 365 OpenAPI is the official Kingsoft Office Open APIs v7 machine contract: 806 paths, 827 operations, and 3,119 schemas
claims.summary: The official OpenAPI 3.0.0 document published at open.wps.cn declares the Kingsoft Office Open APIs v7 contract with 806 paths, 827 operations, and 3,119 schemas; the same document is retained byte-identically in the metadata repository as sources/openapi.yaml.

claims.claim: byte-identical to the spec embedded in the official MIT CLI `@wps365-open/wps365`
claims.summary: The official MIT-licensed CLI package @wps365-open/wps365@0.2.27 embeds the same OpenAPI document (api.yaml); provenance verified the published spec and the package-embedded spec are byte-identical (SHA-256 3a2dfe64...).

claims.claim: The client connects directly to the official production host `https://openapi.wps.cn` (path prefix `/v7`) with the caller's own OAuth2 credentials.
claims.summary: The official OpenAPI document declares the production server url https://openapi.wps.cn with the /v7 path prefix, and WPS 365 requires OAuth2 access-token authentication on every call.

claims.claim: Create an application on the open.wps.cn developer console and apply for the permission scopes each workflow needs.
claims.summary: The official WPS 365 open-platform overview describes registering applications on the WPS open platform and the application permission system (应用权限体系) that binds data-access and interface-call permissions to an application.

claims.claim: Every Endpoint is gated by `kso.*` scopes — for example `kso.calendar_events.readwrite` gates calendar reads and writes.
claims.summary: The OpenAPI document's security schemes enumerate kso.* permission scopes (for example kso.calendar_events.readwrite under the calendar domain) and each operation declares the scopes required per channel.

claims.claim: Use the app channel (client credentials) for server-to-server automation owned by the application, and the delegated channel (authorization code) when acting on behalf of a specific user.
claims.summary: The OpenAPI document declares two OAuth2 security schemes: app uses the clientCredentials flow (application identity access token) and delegated uses the authorizationCode flow (user-authorized access token).

claims.claim: The app and delegated channels can carry different scope sets
claims.summary: Operations declare per-channel security requirements, and the app and delegated schemes expose different scope lists (for example calendar events require kso.calendar_events.readwrite for app but add kso.mcp_* scopes for delegated).

claims.claim: KSO-1 request signing is optional and enabled per application under the developer console security settings.
claims.summary: The official signature documentation states KSO-1 signing is only required when interface signing (接口签名) is enabled under the developer console security settings for the application.

claims.claim: requests must carry the `X-Kso-Date` and `X-Kso-Authorization` headers with an HMAC-SHA256 signature
claims.summary: The official signature documentation specifies the X-Kso-Date and X-Kso-Authorization headers, where the signature value is HMAC-SHA256 computed over "KSO-1" + Method + RequestURI + ContentType + KsoDate + sha256(RequestBody).

claims.claim: 15 operations under `/v7/sse/*` (AIPPT generation, AI docs search, document QA, agent chat) stream `text/event-stream` responses.
claims.summary: The OpenAPI document declares 15 operations under /v7/sse/* (aippt, aidocs, docqa, generator, wps365agent) whose response media type is text/event-stream.

claims.claim: The machine contract enumerates no per-endpoint event names: every event is a JSON payload that carries the type and terminal-state markers.
claims.summary: The official document declares no per-endpoint SSE event names and no stream_status field list; each SSE event carries a JSON payload whose type/terminal discriminator (for example stream_status done or state end) signals completion.

claims.claim: Event subscriptions are encrypted HTTP callbacks pushed by WPS to the caller: each event carries `encrypted_data` plus `signature`, `nonce`, and `iv` fields.
claims.summary: The official event documentation shows WPS pushing subscription events to the subscriber's endpoint and describes the pre-decryption event body (topic, operation, time, nonce, iv, signature, encrypted_data) with a documented decryption algorithm.

claims.claim: Reads are GET and mutations are POST or DELETE only; the official document declares no PUT or PATCH.
claims.summary: The OpenAPI document defines only GET (284), POST (541), and DELETE (1) methods across 826 callable operations and declares no PUT or PATCH anywhere in the contract.
